transcript:
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Windsor Johnston.
President Trump says he rejected Iran's latest proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and
resume nuclear talks.
The offer comes as the two countries are deadlocked over Haut and the conflict.
Iranian President Masoud Pajeshkian tells CBS's Face the Nation that he's reluctant
to meet directly with Trump.
He's heard here through an interpreter.
You see, what the issue is now the atmosphere of distrust that has developed between Iran
and the United States is because we have had several rounds of talks with the United States.
We reached an agreement on the JCPOA and after months of negotiations, the U.S. president
tore it up.
Iran says it could reopen the Strait within a week if the U.S. eases military pressure
and lifts its blockade of Iranian ports.
Iran also says it would allow U.N. nuclear inspectors into the country as part of a longer-term
ceasefire deal.
For now, there's no word on when negotiations will resume.
A massive nor'easter is pounding parts of the Northeast with coastal flooding and strong
winds for a second straight day.
Steve Kestenbaum reports some coastal towns are seeing their worst flooding in more than
a decade.
High tides continue to bring more flooding, especially in towns along the Jersey Shore
In Atlantic City, floodwaters hit their highest level since superstorm Sandy in 2012.
Wind gusts reached 60 miles per hour in some areas.
A public housing employee in New York died when he was hit by a falling tree branch.
Governor Kathy Hochul said dangerous winds will stick around for a while.
It's ferocious and it needs to be taken seriously.
Tens of thousands of power outages were reported from Maine down to North Carolina.
Beach erosion is significant in some areas.
High tides were made worse thanks to Saturday's full moon.
The nor'easter is expected to sit around off the coast of New Jersey and Long Island through
Monday.
For NPR News, I'm Steve Kestenbaum in New York.
Hurricane NOLO is moving away from Hawaii after bringing heavy rain and powerful winds
to the islands.
National Weather Service meteorologist Frank Pereira says some of the storm's effects
will linger.
The system did stay well to the south of the island, and it's going to continue to stay
south as it drifts to west with time over the next day or so.
Now it's going to continue to be some windy conditions across the islands, as well as
some rain bands.
But it does look like the worst of the impacts with that system are over for now.
Farther east in the Pacific, Hurricane Polo is approaching Mexico's Baja California Peninsula.
Others expected to make landfall Monday as a weaker storm.
Polo is also sending dangerous surf toward southern California.
This is NPR News.
A whistleblower says renovations at the Kennedy Center were rushed and some of the work was
poorly done.
The allegations include rusting steel columns and a bathroom floor replaced because President
Trump disliked its color.
The center is now closed for a larger renovation amid a separate fight over Trump's effort
to add his name to the building.
A federal judge has blocked that change, saying it requires congressional approval.
The judge has also ordered the center to give 30 days notice before making major structural
changes.
Police in South Africa say at least 27 people were killed overnight in two separate mass
shootings.
Cape Bartlett says mass shootings there are an increasingly common, with another one reported
earlier this week.
South African police say the first shooting took place at a bar in a township in Johannesburg,
where assailants opened fire with AK-47s.
A separate shooting occurred in a straw near Cape Town.
The shootings come just days after an attack on a house party in the coastal city of Durban
killed 11 people, including a pregnant woman.
South Africa has some of the highest violent crime rates in the world.
Often such mass shooting events are linked to gangs or illegal mining activities.
Cape Bartlett, NPR News, Johannesburg.
The United States and China have agreed to set up a channel for handling incidents involving
artificial intelligence.
The agreement follows three days of talks between President Trump and Chinese President
Xi Jinping in Washington.
I'm Windsor Johnston, NPR News.
